predecessors.name: Sui dynasty
predecessors.text: Beiping, which the Sui general Li Jing could not defend around the new year 619, and Yuyang

successors.name: Tang dynasty
successors.text: Gao's Yan state in northern Hebei: 'his Yan state was also integrated into Tang'

ledger.x: 619: Gao Kaidao declares himself Prince of Yan at Yuyang.
619: Gao takes Beiping from the Sui.
620: Gao Kaidao submits to the Tang.
621: Gao Kaidao rebels against the Tang.
624: Gao's Yan passes to the Tang.
624: Gao Kaidao dies and the Yan state ends.

wars.name: Gao Kaidao's revolt against the Tang
wars.outcome: Gao rebelled in 621, allied himself with the Eastern Turks and Liu Heita, attacked Yi Prefecture (not taken) and, with Jiali Khan and Yuan Junzhang, Yanmen in spring 623 ('could not capture it'); he and the khan took Mayi, which the khan later returned to the…

certainty.note: A warlord's realm in northern Hebei: the page names Beiping, Yuyang, Huairong and Wei Prefecture but no boundary; Cliopatria's shape is the only outline.
